record.evidence_location: Results and discussion, Na diffusion and ionic conductivity section
record.notes: The room-temperature value is extrapolated from the experimental Arrhenius fit, not directly measured at room temperature. The quote is the line-broken sentence 'The high measured experimental values reflects the low ionic conductivity at room temperature 9.4 / 10−16 and 2.0 10−14 S/cm2 for x=0.1 and x=0.30, respectively'; the value 2.0 10−14 maps to x=0.30. The unit as written is S/cm2 (likely a typo for S/cm). The activation energy 1.0 eV for x=0.30 is from the sentence 'the experimental one is of 0.95 eV and 1.0 eV for x=0.1 and x=0.30'. The paper's conductivity wording refers to 'electronic conductivity (S/cm)' in the methods but the context is ionic. The x=0.10 value (9.4 10−16 S/cm) was omitted because its number is split across a line break in the PDF text and could not be quoted verbatim. Density and sintering fields are not applicable because the glass was melt-quenched and the density given is measured, not relative.
